macos.rationale: Buzz 1.0.6 ships macos desktop builds; macOS minimum 12.0, Windows x64 unsigned and Linux x64 deb/AppImage retain their stated release limits.

windows.rationale: Buzz 1.0.6 ships windows desktop builds; macOS minimum 12.0, Windows x64 unsigned and Linux x64 deb/AppImage retain their stated release limits.

linux.rationale: Buzz 1.0.6 ships linux desktop builds; macOS minimum 12.0, Windows x64 unsigned and Linux x64 deb/AppImage retain their stated release limits.

web-client.rationale: The inspected release supplies desktop/mobile clients; browser-host is explicitly development/test tooling and rejects a production browser backend configuration.

ios.rationale: Current first-party support lists iPhone and Android apps and identity pairing. Store-region/device limits apply; local agents still need their host awake.

android.rationale: Current first-party support lists iPhone and Android apps and identity pairing. Store-region/device limits apply; local agents still need their host awake.

mobile-web.rationale: No production mobile-browser client is supplied in the scoped release; its Node browser host is explicitly for development/tests.

cli.rationale: Buzz 1.0.6 bundles the product-owned buzz CLI from block/buzz revision 630922a, separately from coding-harness CLIs.

claude-code.rationale: The v1.0.6 registry ships claude-code; Pi is opt-in and Claude/Codex require macOS/Linux. Generic plugin registration is a separate mechanism.

codex.rationale: The v1.0.6 registry ships codex; Pi is opt-in and Claude/Codex require macOS/Linux. Generic plugin registration is a separate mechanism.

cursor.rationale: Bounded inspection of the v1.0.6 bundled/organization registry and runtime registrations finds no shipped cursor adapter. 0.X ACP presets and model names are not current harness support; custom plugins do not establish a named integration.

gemini-cli.rationale: Bounded inspection of the v1.0.6 bundled/organization registry and runtime registrations finds no shipped gemini-cli adapter. 0.X ACP presets and model names are not current harness support; custom plugins do not establish a named integration.

opencode.rationale: Bounded inspection of the v1.0.6 bundled/organization registry and runtime registrations finds no shipped opencode adapter. 0.X ACP presets and model names are not current harness support; custom plugins do not establish a named integration.

pi.rationale: The v1.0.6 registry ships pi; Pi is opt-in and Claude/Codex require macOS/Linux. Generic plugin registration is a separate mechanism.

grok.rationale: Bounded inspection of the v1.0.6 bundled/organization registry and runtime registrations finds no shipped grok adapter. 0.X ACP presets and model names are not current harness support; custom plugins do not establish a named integration.

aider.rationale: Bounded inspection of the v1.0.6 bundled/organization registry and runtime registrations finds no shipped aider adapter. 0.X ACP presets and model names are not current harness support; custom plugins do not establish a named integration.

antigravity.rationale: Bounded inspection of the v1.0.6 bundled/organization registry and runtime registrations finds no shipped antigravity adapter. 0.X ACP presets and model names are not current harness support; custom plugins do not establish a named integration.

byo-subscription.rationale: The current desktop uses Claude account and Codex ChatGPT/OpenAI sign-in; old standalone buzz-acp API-key-only instructions do not restrict these native routes.

local.rationale: Local harnesses run on the Buzz computer while the app is running.

vendor-cloud.rationale: Builderlab hosted agents run on vendor workstations, paid from workspace funds; paid-service US/account eligibility restrictions apply.

worktree.rationale: Work in a new worktree uses a separate worktree/branch for local code changes. This is file separation, not a sandbox.

parallel-runs.rationale: Independent agents can work concurrently; each local runner also has one mention lane plus up to eight Interest lanes. This is source-established capacity, not an observed benchmark.

coordinator.rationale: Buzz ships delegation/callback instructions and messaging tools for an agent to assign/inspect available sibling-agent work in a shared channel. Verified common-owner authority applies, and creating agents still needs owner review.

issue-tracking.rationale: The CLI actually bundled with v1.0.6 creates persistent native relay issues with stable IDs, assignments and status, separate from chat/session records. The 1.0 desktop has no native issue editor; this receipt establishes CLI scope only.

unattended-triggers.rationale: Relay workflows and local Attention can start work from schedules/events; local Attention requires the app host running, unlike hosted agents/relay automation.

roles.rationale: Community/channel Owner/Admin/member access and Builderlab workspace admin controls have distinct permissions; private channel access remains independent of billing/admin status.

sso.rationale: Enterprise explicitly advertises SSO; this does not claim SSO on every local/self-host deployment or a public Enterprise price.

pr-workflow.rationale: The 1.0 GitHub panel manages reviews, checks and merge/queue actions through gh; bundled CLI native relay PR records are a separate backend.

review-ui.rationale: The 1.0 app shows GitHub PR diffs/checks/reviews and opt-in local per-turn Changesets cards; remote/concurrent-writer attribution limits apply.

license.rationale: The main buzz-app v1.0.6 application is Apache-2.0 with third-party notices. Closed hosted components are not assigned that license by inference.

self-hosting.rationale: The 1.0 app can use an independently hosted open-source relay; local agents and key identity do not require Builderlab-hosted control services.

free-tier.rationale: Community/local software is free and Pay as you go starts with a recurring data allowance and no payment method; provider/hosted-compute charges remain separate.

starting-price.rationale: The lowest ADE access price is free Community/local software or a free initial Pay as you go workspace, excluding provider and paid hosted usage.

no-paid-plan.rationale: Builderlab has paid usage and an Enterprise offer beside free local software; the whole product is not an ADE with no paid tier.

free-plan.rationale: Free Community/local software and a recurring free hosted allowance coexist with paid Builderlab usage/Enterprise.

subscription.rationale: The complete posted plan list has free Community, prepaid Pay as you go with no recurring platform payment, and a custom Enterprise commitment; it offers no standard recurring individual/flat subscription. Enterprise terms are negotiated.

per-seat.rationale: The complete public plan list bills Pay as you go through pooled workspace usage, not seats, and publishes no per-seat Enterprise price; negotiated Enterprise terms remain separate.

usage-based.rationale: Builderlab deducts metered inference, data and remote-compute consumption from prepaid workspace funds.

compute.rationale: Hosted remote-agent compute is $0.65 per vCPU-hour while running, metered to the second; this is an ADE-operated compute charge.

byok.rationale: Local/connected harnesses accept the user’s provider sign-in or key; their provider bills separately from Builderlab funds.

one-time.rationale: The complete public offer consists of free software, metered prepaid services and negotiated Enterprise terms. A $5-$1,000 top-up funds consumption and buys no perpetual one-time software licence.

laptop-independent.rationale: Builderlab hosted agents are documented to answer with the desktop off, subject to funds/eligibility and workstation idle suspension. Local same-host agents are excluded from this receipt.
